title: Removing the lead unassigns the lines that followed it and leaves the rest
custom_preconds:
1. You are signed in on the Work Orders build under test with Work Orders view permission and Work Orders create-and-edit; the Board View and Tech View display options are on.
  2. The current location has at least 3 lead technicians shown as groups/columns (a technician is eligible when they are Clockable, Active, and their role is not Office or Time Clock User).
  3. Via New Work Order, create several work orders and set a Lead Technician on each, spread across the technicians with some left Unassigned; then open the Work Orders page.
  4. A work order led by technician A with the same six line types as the assign case.
custom_steps:
1. Reassign the work order to Unassigned.
  2. Open the work order and check each line:
  3. - the no-tech line and the implicit-lead line are now unassigned;
  4. - explicit, Complete, logged-labor, and active-clock lines are unchanged.
custom_expected:
Expected results

  • You can change the lead while the outgoing lead is clocked into a work-order line.
  • An actively clocked-in line keeps its assigned technician, even when that assignment is implicit or has no earlier logged labor.

Source — where this behaviour comes from
Epic SV-10043 (Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options). Story reference: SV-10047 — Story 4 Reassign or unassign the lead technician. Spec: Confluence page 845185030 “Work Orders — Board View & Tech View Display Options (Draft Spec)”, Draft v0.9, requirement(s) S4-E1, S4-E6 (read 23 Sep 2026). Review decisions/answers: Confluence page 853901313 where cited. Source-verified on 23 September 2026; not yet build-verified.

Exact quotes from the source (for reproducibility)

  • S4-E1: “Allow lead changes while the outgoing lead is clocked into a work order line.”
  • S4-E6: “An actively clocked-in line retains its assigned technician, even if assignment is implicit or no earlier labor exists.”
